sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — of Phosphatotitan was found in the Sidi Chennane phosphate mine in Morocco. It is a fragmentary skeleton containing dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebrae along with parts of the pelvis.
This dinosaur measured approximately 39.75% the linear dimensions of Patagotitan and is estimated to have weighed between 3.5 and 4.3 tonnes.
To date, only one fossil occurrence of Phosphatotitan has been recorded.
Researchers suggest that Phosphatotitan's small size may be due to island dwarfism or environmental conditions favoring smaller herbivores in the latest Cretaceous.
Phosphatotitan is classified as a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur within the family Argentinosauridae. It belongs to the clade Lognkosauria, which otherwise contains only South American members.
Phosphatotitan lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
It is debated whether the relationship between Moroccan and South American titanosaurs reflects ancient wide distribution or complex oceanic dispersal patterns.
